The use of instrumental variables allowed us to demonstrate a significant relationship between better ambulatory process of care and better health-related quality of life outcomes for patients with chronic disease. This finding underscores the importance of efforts to improve the process of care, suggesting that improving ambulatory care can lead to better overall well-being for individuals with chronic conditions.

In other words, when healthcare providers focus on providing high-quality care in a timely manner, it can have a positive impact on patients' health-related quality of life outcomes. This implies that investing in processes like medication management, follow-up appointments, and addressing complications promptly can contribute to better long-term health outcomes for individuals with chronic disease.

While the results suggest that improved ambulatory process of care is associated with better health-related quality of life outcomes, it's essential to note that other factors also play a role. Patients' self-reported health-related quality of life can provide valuable prognostic information regarding survival in certain conditions, such as non-small-cell lung cancer.

Overall, the findings highlight the importance of considering ambulatory process of care when evaluating the effectiveness of healthcare interventions for patients with chronic disease. By prioritizing efficient and effective care delivery, we may be able to improve health outcomes and overall quality of life for these individuals.
